facts.statement: Under functional gradient flow, the MeanFlow and Lagrangian objectives converge pointwise to the true flow map.
MeanFlow closed form: the learned map follows the true flow up to t_τ, then the initial map; t_τ increases from s to t.
Lagrangian closed form: the learned map follows the initial map up to s_τ, then the true flow; s_τ decreases from t to s.
MeanFlow error decays exponentially in optimization time.
Synthetic setup used to validate Theorem 1.
On synthetic data, the learned average velocities match the closed forms of Theorem 1.
For every step size η and every ε, some initial error smaller than ε makes gradient descent diverge (MeanFlow; Lagrangian with v = 0).
Counterexample: error ε(t−s)^m is multiplied by (1 − η(m+1)) at each step and diverges when η(m+1) > 2.
Normalized update divides the residual by (‖r‖² + c)^p.
For p ≥ 0.5 the normalized updates have uniformly bounded norms.
p = 1 yields convergence of MeanFlow to a neighborhood of the solution, of size O(η^(1/2)).
p = 1.0 is the value found to work best for from-scratch training on ImageNet 256×256 in the original MeanFlow paper.
